question: Deti zo seriálu Stranger Things pomenujú tajomné monštrum podľa démona z hry Dungeons & Dragons, ktorú práve hrajú. Ako sa to monštrum volá?
source_excerpt: the Demogorgon is actually the name of a chaotic evil beast found in the tabletop game Dungeons and Dragons beginning with the Eldritch Wizardry book in 1976.

extra.why_interesting: Millions of viewers know the monster's name but assume the show invented it. It is actually a classic demon from the D&D rulebooks, which the kids borrow from the game they are playing at the kitchen table.
extra.verification_notes: In season 1 the boys name the creature Demogorgon after the D&D demon lord during their game; no later development contradicts this (https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/87800/otherworldly-history-demogorgon).

explanation: Demogorgon je v Dungeons & Dragons obávané knieža démonov už od sedemdesiatych rokov. Chlapci v seriáli si jeho meno jednoducho požičali z hracieho stola.

question: Na obyčajnej hracej kocke dávajú protiľahlé steny dokopy vždy sedem. Hráči Dungeons & Dragons hádžu dvadsaťstennou kockou, ktorá dodržiava rovnaké pravidlo. Koľko dávajú dokopy jej protiľahlé steny?
source_excerpt: dice are traditionally numbered such that the largest number is located opposite the smallest

extra.why_interesting: Most people know that opposite faces of an ordinary die add up to seven, but few realise the iconic D&D d20 follows the same hidden rule. Players can work it out from the pattern (6+1, so 20+1) and get a satisfying 'I worked it out!' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Standard d20 convention has opposite faces summing to 21 (1 opposite 20), and the question's premise that it follows the same rule excludes non-standard numberings; support is from dice-seller pages and an NRICH puzzle, not an encyclopedic source.

explanation: Platí to isté ako pri bežnej kocke: protiľahlé čísla dávajú dokopy počet stien plus jeden. Vďaka tomu sú vysoké a nízke čísla rozložené rovnomerne a kocka nenadŕža žiadnej strane.
